A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GestureLSM and contain 13 readable pages, including Appendices A–E. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original BEAT2 experiments, a 20-participant user study, ablations in Tables 2–3 and training analysis in Figure 9.

after.justification: v4 retains the original BEAT2 results, user study, main-text and appendix ablations, and training analysis.

M1.justification: Both retain the same regional RVQ representation, spatial-then-temporal attention, speech conditioning, latent shortcut learning and beta-distribution timestep sampling in Section 3.

E1.justification: Both use BEAT2 for speech-conditioned body and facial gesture generation and retain the same avatar-generation demonstrations. No dataset, task or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in Table 1, the Section 4.3 user study, and the generator and acceleration comparisons in Table 2.

E3.justification: The EMAGE data split, evaluation metrics, training budgets, default eight-step inference and randomized 20-participant/320-video user-study protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the same component, architecture, sampling, guidance and representation ablations. The denoising analysis, qualitative examples and Appendix E training analysis also match.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including Figure 7's error bars. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed details or significance tests.

E6.justification: All table entries and plotted or qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains GestureLSM FGD 4.088 and GestureLSM (+ Face) FGD 4.247; Tables 2–3 also retain every ablation result.

T1.justification: The quantization, attention, flow-matching, shortcut and beta-distribution formulations in Section 3 are unchanged, as are the metric definitions in Appendix C.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about coherent full-body gestures, real-time generation and state-of-the-art BEAT2 performance.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and experimental interpretations match, including Appendix E's qualification that higher beat constancy can reflect unnatural motion and should be judged against ground truth.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same codebook specifications, layer counts, optimizer, training durations, A100 hardware and guidance settings. The abstract provides the same project-page link.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and all 66 reference entries are unchanged in substance. Positioning relative to earlier gesture-generation, flow-matching and shortcut methods remains identical.

P1.justification: v4 adds Junfan Zhu to the author list and University of Chicago to the affiliations, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section/appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–3 retain their contents, captions, axes, legends, arrangement and placement. The page layout is preserved without figure or table redesign or relocation.

improvement.justification: The revisions concern authorship, affiliation and version metadata. Scientific exposition, empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful net change in paper quality.
